title: Policy Targeting with Binary Classification Trees: an Application to Rural Hospital Closures
abstract: arXiv:2609.13068v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Empirical researchers often use binary classification trees to identify subgroups at risk of adverse outcomes. We compare two classification tree algorithms in this policy-targeting context: classical classification and regression trees (CART) and the maximizing-distance final-split approach (MDFS). We establish a theoretical setting in which MDFS identifies a high-risk subgroup while CART identifies none. Applied to rural hospital closure data, MDFS targets a high-closure-probability subgroup: for-profit hospitals with more than 63 days in accounts receivable. CART misses this subgroup. To facilitate further application of these classification tree algorithms, we provide \texttt{targetree} package in Python, R, and Stata.

translated_title: 基于二元分类树的政策瞄准：在农村医院关闭中的应用
translated_abstract: 实证研究者经常使用二元分类树来识别面临不良后果风险的子群体。我们在政策瞄准的背景下比较了两种分类树算法：经典的分类与回归树（CART）和最大化距离最终分裂方法（MDFS）。我们建立了一个理论情境，在该情境下MDFS能够识别出高风险子群体，而CART则无法识别。应用于农村医院关闭数据时，MDFS成功瞄准了一个高关闭概率的子群体：应收账款天数超过63天的营利性医院，而CART则遗漏了这一子群体。为了促进这些分类树算法的进一步应用，我们提供了Python、R和Stata版本的targetree软件包。
tldr: 该研究比较了CART与MDFS两种分类树算法在政策瞄准中的表现，从理论和实证上证明MDFS能识别出CART遗漏的高风险子群体，并发现应收账款超过63天的营利性医院是农村医院关闭的高风险群体。
en_tdlr: This study compares CART and MDFS classification tree algorithms for policy targeting, theoretically and empirically demonstrating that MDFS identifies high-risk subgroups that CART misses, and finding that for-profit hospitals with over 63 days in accounts receivable are at high risk of rural closure.
